headline: High: Goose’s default filesystem and shell access can conflict with a local game-playing agent, while prompt-injection and leakage risks are limited by the game agent’s lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A shows no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot readily ingest Goose output by default. Goose can read files, use MCP, and write the filesystem, so a manual or file-based bridge could still carry injected content into A if the operator creates one. This is a limited, non-default pathway.
conditions: IF the operator copies Goose-generated text into a file or prompt consumed by agent_a
IF agent_b writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file that agent_a later reads
mitigations: Keep agent_a isolated from shared files
Disable shared MCP endpoints for this pair
Review any copied text before feeding it to agent_a

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write the user filesystem and handle source code, while agent A touches no data classes and has no network egress. That makes broad leakage from A to B unlikely, but B can still expose any shared local files it accesses. The pair does not show a default path for sensitive data exfiltration from A.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the same cwd that agent_b can read
IF agent_b is given credentials or secrets in its workspace
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside the shared cwd
Remove secrets from the workspace before running Goose
Use a dedicated non-sensitive project directory
Rotate any credentials exposed to agent_b

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; agent A is a game-playing agent with no stated write or network capabilities. The conflict is one-sided rather than symmetric, but Goose’s default mutable access can still collide with any files or state A relies on if they share a workspace. Uncertainty about A’s hidden workspace makes medium the safer choice.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same filesystem path
IF Goose modifies git state in a repo that agent_a also reads
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Avoid pointing Goose at repositories used by agent_a
Disable git writes for Goose during parallel runs
Snapshot the workspace before starting both agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on tool outputs and modify files or git state, so if it consumes agent A’s outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into real actions. Agent A is a game-playing agent, which lowers the chance of high-stakes downstream harm, but the pair still supports an A-to-B trust chain without a built-in verification step. That is a default-unsafe inference path.
conditions: IF Goose uses agent_a output as a source of facts or instructions
IF Goose is allowed to commit or execute actions based on that output
mitigations: Require manual review before Goose acts on agent_a output
Insert a verification step between agents
Disable commit or shell actions for the session
Limit agent_a output to non-authoritative summaries

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated handling is documented for agent A, and agent B only lists source code and files in cwd. Without PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy evidence, the rubric’s compliance pathways are not established. I cite both profiles because the absence of regulated data on A and the limited data classes on B jointly block the listed compliance triggers.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the shared workspace
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair
Use a separate compliant environment for regulated workloads
Document retention and residency rules before enabling the pair
